chapter: Dancing schools and Charlie Johnson in New York
title: June Clark's band at the Club Kentucky
summary: After the dancing school the band followed Duke Ellington into the mob-run Club Kentucky at 49th and Broadway, where the gangsters treated musicians well.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: that Duke was playing downtown? (Inaudible) tell you what it is and it goes away. Cut it off and I'll get --
Okay. We're talking about the Club Kentucky.
You were with June Clark at this time?

Yeah. This is around about '32. It was in the early 30's. Around about '32, 1932. I think it was the winter. That was the year, the first year. If you know the date that Duke went to the Cotton Club, that is the -- We followed Duke into that little club. Duke left and we came into the Club Kentucky. That was 49th Street and Broadway, down in the basement there. And we worked in there. It was run by a bunch of gangsters. Yeah, the mob had that. They were something else. But they always treated the musicians right. I never had no

trouble out of them. We used to play all their parties for them.
While we went in there, Duke went to the Cotton Club in Harlem. That was the years he formed that big band (inaudible).

And he had most of the guys, the rhythm section and everything, three or four horns. But I know he went in the Cotton Club. I know all the people he (Inaudible) got together with him when he opened at the Cotton Club.
We stayed down -- we came in and took over the Club Kentucky.
June, the following year, there was a show called Just A Minute, and they had musicians and they had a band on the stage.

And June Clark doubled -- just June himself, not the band he had in the club -- just June Clark himself (inaudible) got the job in Just A Minute. Trumpet player -- he played the trumpet. He played spots (inaudible).
